items.title: Political parties should move towards open primaries to deepen internal democracy – Prof Kwasi Prempeh
items.description: Chairman of the Constitutional Review Committee, Prof Henry Kwasi Prempeh, has renewed calls for Ghana’s political parties to gradually abandon the delegate system in favour of more open and participatory primary elections, arguing that such a move would strengthen internal democracy and better reflect the principles of democratic governance. Speaking in an interview with Accra-based Woezor TV, Professor Prempeh said although the delegate system has long been the preferred method for selecting parliamentary and presidential candidates within the major political parties, developments over the years suggest that the parties themselves recognise the need for broader participation by their membership. According to him, the evolution of delegate numbers in recent election cycles demonstrates a growing acceptance within the political parties that the current system should become more inclusive. “I think a lot has been said about the delegate system, often very critically,” Professor Prempeh observed. “You can tell even the way the numbers have evolved. The parties themselves have been growing the numbers incrementally.” Professor Prempeh noted that both major political parties have gradually increased the size of their electoral colleges over time, allowing more delegates to participate in the selection of party leaders and parliamentary candidates. He argued that this gradual expansion reflects an acknowledgement by the parties that broader participation enhances the legitimacy of internal elections. The Constitutional Review Committee Chairman explained that the trend suggests an underlying desire to move away from a system in which relatively small groups of delegates determine the political fortunes of aspiring candidates. Instead, he believes the logical progression is towards a system in which ordinary party members are empowered to vote directly in primary elections. “There’s a certain impulse within the parties themselves that they need somehow to move towards open primaries where members will participate,” he said. Professor Prempeh pointed to an earlier attempt by one of Ghana’s major political parties, the National Democratic Congress (NDC), to significantly expand participation in its internal elections. According to him, the party at one stage sought to extend voting rights to almost its entire membership before later reversing that decision. He explained that discussions with party officials at the time suggested the retreat was influenced less by opposition to wider participation than by concerns over political competitiveness. “The sense was that if we do it alone and the other party doesn’t reciprocate, then it’s almost like we are placing ourselves at a disadvantage,” he recounted. Professor Prempeh maintained that open primaries, in which all registered party members participate in selecting candidates, represent a more democratic approach to internal party governance. He argued that political parties, as institutions central to Ghana’s democratic system, should themselves operate according to democratic principles. “That is more democratic. That is really what a fully fledged democratic party should do,” he stated. He indicated that allowing the wider party membership to determine candidates would strengthen transparency, improve accountability and enhance the legitimacy of those elected to represent the parties. The committee has been consulting political parties, civil society organisations, traditional authorities, professional bodies and members of the public on a range of constitutional and governance issues. Professor Prempeh acknowledged that any transition from delegate-based elections to open primaries would require careful planning and broad consensus among the political parties.

items.title: INEC’s job is to publish names, not vet candidates — Adebayo
items.description: By Efe Onodjae The Social Democratic Party (SDP) presidential candidate, Adewale Adebayo, has said the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is responsible for publishing the names of candidates submitted by political parties, not determining their eligibility. Speaking on Sunday Politics, Adebayo described INEC as a public institution whose duty is to receive and make candidates’ information available to Nigerians, stressing that the commission is not responsible for verifying the accuracy of credentials submitted by aspirants. “INEC is our servant. It’s working for the public. INEC is just like the post office. Its role is to collect the information submitted by political parties and candidates and make it available to the electorate. It’s not INEC’s job to vet the information,” he said. According to him, it is the responsibility of the electorate and other stakeholders to scrutinise candidates’ claims and challenge any false declarations through the appropriate legal channels. On the publication of his name as the SDP’s presidential candidate, Adebayo dismissed reports of a crisis within the party, insisting the SDP’s nomination process was peaceful and transparent. He noted that alongside his name, INEC also published the names of the party’s vice-presidential candidate, 109 senatorial candidates and 360 House of Representatives candidates, describing the exercise as routine. Adebayo urged Nigerians to focus less on political intrigues and more on issues affecting the country, including poverty, insecurity, poor governance and economic challenges, ahead of the 2027 general elections. items.title: 2027: Kwara APC chair mocks opposition over internal crises
items.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The Kwara State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Prince Sunday Fagbemi, has criticised opposition parties in the state over what he described as unresolved internal crises surrounding their governorship candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. Fagbemi said while the APC had successfully concluded its candidate selection process, some opposition parties were still struggling with disputes over the emergence of their candidates despite the timetable released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). He spoke on Sunday during a visit by APC candidates to communities in Kwara South to appreciate party members for their support and commitment during the recently concluded primaries. According to him, some political parties were yet to resolve disagreements arising from the emergence of multiple governorship candidates, even after the deadline for submission of candidates. Speaking during visits to Ilemona, Erin-Ile and Offa, Fagbemi said residents of Kwara South had remained loyal to the APC, contributing to the successful conduct of the party’s primaries, which produced candidates for various elective positions, including its governorship candidate, Mr Salihu Yakubu-Danladi. “Our purpose of coming here is to thank the people of Oyun and Offa Local Government Areas for standing firmly with the party during the primaries that produced our candidates. “We appreciate your steadfastness, commitment and loyalty to the APC. We could not take your support for granted, which is why we deemed it necessary to return and express our gratitude,” he said. Fagbemi said the APC governorship candidate, senatorial candidate, House of Representatives candidates and House of Assembly candidates joined the visit to personally thank party members and stakeholders for their support. He added that the delegation also visited traditional rulers in the area to seek their blessings and appreciate their contributions to peace and democratic development. The Onipe of Ipe, Oba Mufutau Lawal, who spoke on behalf of traditional rulers in the area, commended Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq for what he described as significant developmental achievements across the state. The monarch urged APC candidates to justify the confidence placed in them if elected and offered prayers for their success in the forthcoming elections. Oba Lawal also reaffirmed the support of the people of Kwara South for the APC and pledged their commitment to the party’s candidates. The post 2027: Kwara APC chair mocks opposition over internal crises appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Face à la canicule, Général Emballage adapte ses horaires
items.description: On parle beaucoup de la canicule en Algérie depuis quelques semaines mais sans doute peu de son effet sur la sphère industrielle. Pourtant, comme tout autre secteur, l’industrie subit elle aussi l’impact des fortes chaleurs. Pour les atténuer, Général Emballage, leader algérien du carton ondulé, a pris des dispositions. Général Emballage : la santé des travailleurs au cœur des priorités L’objectif de l'entreprise basée à Akbou (Béjaïa) est double : protéger à la fois la santé de ses personnels et la productivité de ses unités. “ Parce qu'une industrie performante est avant tout une industrie qui place l'humain au cœur de ses priorités ”, met en avant l’entreprise. Au-delà d’une température d'environ 32 °C, chaque degré supplémentaire peut entraîner une baisse de productivité estimée entre 2 et 5 %, indique Général Emballage sur son site Internet, citant les chiffres de l'Organisation internationale du Travail (OIT). Néanmoins, précise l’entreprise, “avant d'être un enjeu de performance, la chaleur est avant tout un enjeu de santé et de sécurité au travail ”. “ Lorsque les températures augmentent, la sécurité de nos collaborateurs reste notre priorité ”, insiste-t-elle. Général emballage est basée à Akbou et possède des unités à Sétif et Oran, en plus de sa grande usine de fabrication de carton en construction à Naâma. Canicule : Général Emballage supprime la tranche horaire de travail 13-21 h À Akbou, face aux épisodes de canicule ayant touché la région, Général Emballage indique avoir adapté son organisation. Elle a mis en place un système de travail 2×8 continu et supprimé la plage horaire la plus exposée à la chaleur, soit entre 13 h et 21 h. Selon les explications fournies, cette mesure vise à limiter l'exposition des travailleurs aux fortes chaleurs, préserver des conditions de travail plus sûres, garantir la continuité de la production et maintenir la qualité des produits de l'entreprise (emballages), également affectée par les températures extrêmes. Des dispositifs complémentaires ont été déployés sur les sites de Sétif et d'Oran, tels que la brumisation et le renforcement de l'approvisionnement en eau, afin d’améliorer les conditions de travail, fait savoir en outre Général Emballage. L’article Face à la canicule, Général Emballage adapte ses horaires est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Championnat national de horse-ball 2026 / Phase Maritime : Hyman Hippique Club de Lomé s’impose aux tirs au but (1-0) en match inaugural
items.description: Lomé, 2 août (ATOP) – Hyman Hippique Club de Lomé a remporté le match inaugural de la phase Maritime des éliminatoires du championnat national de horse-ball 2026, le samedi 1 er août sur les installations de Sarakawa à Lomé. Il s’est imposé face au Club des Nations de Lomé aux tirs au but (1-0), après un nul de 1 but partout. Coup d’envoi du championnat Le coup d’envoi de cette rencontre, disputée en deux périodes de dix minutes (10 mn x 2), a été donné par le président de la Fédération des sports équestres du Togo (Fe.S.E.T), Téouri Hyman. C’était en présence de plusieurs personnalités de la préfecture de Tchaoudjo, gardiennes de la tradition équestre. Habitués à partager les mêmes installations d’entraînement, les deux clubs loméens se connaissaient parfaitement. Ils ont ainsi entamé la rencontre sans phase d’observation, chacun cherchant à prendre rapidement l’ascendant sur son adversaire. L’engagement physique a entraîné quelques échanges musclés, nécessitant l’intervention de l’arbitre central pour ramener le calme. Profitant ensuite d’un jeu plus posé, Hyman Hippique Club de Lomé a développé de belles séquences de passes courtes avant d’ouvrir le score à la 5ᵉ minute grâce à Jacob. Il conserve cet avantage jusqu’à la pause. Au retour des vestiaires, le Club des Nations est revenu avec de meilleures intentions. Plus entreprenants, ses joueurs ont progressivement repris le contrôle du jeu avant d’égaliser à la 18ᵉ minute par l’intermédiaire de Salissou. Malgré plusieurs occasions de part et d’autre, le score est resté inchangé jusqu’au coup de sifflet final (1-1). La qualification s’est donc jouée lors de la séance des tirs au but, où Hyman Hippique Club de Lomé s’est montré plus efficace en transformant son tir, tandis que le Club des Nations a échoué dans cet exercice, offrant ainsi la victoire à Hyman Hippique Club (1-0). Transformation du penalty Le championnat national de horse-ball 2026 se dispute, comme les éditions précédentes, en deux étapes. La phase Maritime regroupe les clubs de Lomé, d’Aného et de Kpalimé, soit un total de huit équipes. La seconde phase se déroulera à Sokodé et mettra aux prises les clubs de Tchamba, Blitta, Kara, Dapaong ainsi que ceux de Sokodé. Le président de la Fe.S.E.T a fait savoir que les trois meilleures équipes de chacune des deux phases seront qualifiées pour la phase finale à Lomé. Elles seront réparties en deux poules, dont les vainqueurs s’affronteront en finale nationale afin de désigner le champion du Togo de Horse-Ball 2026, a indiqué Téouri Hyman. ATOP/AR/AO/KYA

items.title: Olowu Kuta to Olowu of Owu Abeokuta: Your reign continues to attract admiration, respect across Nigeria
items.description: By Matthew Johnson The Olowu of Kuta Kingdom, His Royal Majesty Oba Hameed Makama Oyelude, Tegbosun III, has congratulated the Olowu of Owu Abeokuta, Oba Saka Adelola Matemilola, Olúyálọ̀ Ọ̀tílẹ́ta VII, on the occasion of his coronation anniversary. In a congratulatory message, Oba Oyelude described the celebration as a testament to God’s grace and the remarkable leadership that has characterised the reign of the Olowu of Owu Abeokuta since his ascension to the throne. The monarch commended Oba Matemilola for his unwavering commitment to promoting peace, unity, cultural heritage and sustainable development in Owu Abeokuta, noting that his reign has “continued to attract admiration and respect across Nigeria and beyond.” Oba Oyelude prayed that “Almighty God would grant the Olowu of Owu Abeokuta many more years in good health, divine wisdom and renewed strength to continue providing purposeful leadership for the people of Owu Abeokuta and contributing meaningfully to national development.” He wished the Olowu of Owu Abeokuta “a joyous coronation celebration and reaffirmed the enduring bond of brotherhood among traditional rulers committed to preserving the rich Yoruba cultural heritage, fostering peaceful coexistence and advancing the development of their respective communities.” The Olowu of Kuta further expressed confidence that the reign of the Olowu of Owu Abeokuta “would continue to usher in greater peace, progress and prosperity for Owu Abeokuta, while inspiring future generations through exemplary traditional leadership.” The post Olowu Kuta to Olowu of Owu Abeokuta: Your reign continues to attract admiration, respect across Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: South-East security: Militants surrender arms as troops recover weapons
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Following sustained military operations by troops of the 82 Division/Joint Task Force South-East, Operation Udoka, several members of militant groups have surrendered their arms, while intelligence-led operations have led to the recovery of additional weapons and an Improvised Explosive Device (IED). The Nigerian Army, in a statement on Sunday, said the development highlights the effectiveness of its integrated kinetic and non-kinetic approach towards dismantling criminal networks and restoring peace across the region. According to the statement, the breakthrough followed sustained pressure by troops of the 34 Artillery Brigade and the recent arrest of suspects linked to the killing of a soldier. “Unable to withstand the relentless military offensive, members of a militant group operating within Egbema and its environs voluntarily began surrendering their weapons,” the Army said. It added that one of the suspects disclosed the location where the group’s weapons were concealed, leading security operatives to recover the arms. Items recovered included one AK-47 rifle, two AK-47 magazines, 54 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition and four locally fabricated firearms. In a related development, troops of Sector 5, Operation Udo Ka, acting on credible intelligence, recovered two General Purpose Machine Guns (GPMGs), 45 rounds of 7.62mm x 51 ammunition and one IED. The Army said the recovery had further degraded the capacity of criminal elements to threaten public safety in the region. It described the surrender of arms as evidence that sustained operational pressure, supported by strategic engagements and collaboration with other security agencies, was compelling criminal elements to abandon violence. “The Nigerian Army remains resolute in sustaining the current operational momentum until all criminal networks are dismantled and enduring peace and stability are fully restored across the South-East,” the statement added. The Army reiterated its commitment to protecting Nigeria’s sovereignty and safeguarding the lives and property of citizens through intelligence-driven operations conducted in collaboration with other security agencies and stakeholders. It urged members of the public to continue providing credible information to security agencies, noting that public support remains vital to sustaining security gains. items.title: Journée internationale de la femme africaine : Le gouvernement renforce l’autonomisation économique des femmes agricultrices
items.description: Djarkpanga, 2 août (ATOP) – L’apothéose de la 64ᵉ édition de la Journée internationale de la femme africaine s’est déroulée, le vendredi 31 juillet à Djarkpanga, préfecture de Mô sous le thème national « Femmes entrepreneures togolaises : lever les barrières et accélérer les opportunités ». La célébration a permis au ministère en charge des Solidarités et du Genre, soutenu par le Fonds des nations unies pour les populations (UNFPA), de remettre des matériels composés de 10 tricycles, 2 égreneuses et 5 motopompes à 12 organisations paysannes féminines. Ces équipements sont destinés à améliorer leurs capacités de production, de transformation et de commercialisation des produits agricoles en vue de renforcer leur autonomisation économique. La cérémonie a été, également, marquée par des prestations culturelles et des sensibilisations sur le thème. Les messages ont mis en lumière le rôle essentiel des femmes dans le développement local, la cohésion sociale et la sécurité alimentaire. Vue partielle des matériels La ministre chargée des Solidarités et du Genre, Mme Moni Sankarédja-Sinandja a présidé les manifestations en présence des autorités administratives, politiques, traditionnelles, religieuses ainsi que d’une forte mobilisation des femmes de la préfecture. Elle a fait savoir que le thème national traduit la volonté commune de créer un environnement plus favorable à l’épanouissement économique des femmes. Mme Sankarédja-Sinandja a indiqué que malgré leur engagement remarquable, les femmes demeurent confrontées à plusieurs obstacles, notamment l’accès limité au financement, aux équipements modernes, aux marchés, au foncier et aux opportunités de formation. La ministre a fait savoir que lever ces barrières constitue une priorité pour le gouvernement, en ajoutant que l’exécutif poursuit ses actions de proximité en faveur des groupements féminins. La chargée de programme Genre et Droits humains, Violences basées sur le genre (VBG) à l’UNFPA, Mme Letou Agossou Améyo a salué cette célébration puis réitéré la disponibilité du Fonds à accompagner le Togo dans ses efforts visant à lever les barrières et à accélérer les opportunités aux femmes. Elle a précisé que le partenariat avec le ministère en charge des Solidarités et du Genre pour l’octroi des matériels aux groupements féminins symbolise l’engagement concret de l’UNFPA, celui de donner les moyens à la femme agricultrice de passer de la subsistance à l’entrepreneuriat. Le préfet de Tchaoudjo, assumant les fonctions de gouverneur de la région Centrale, Tchimbiandja Yendoukoa Douti, a rendu hommage au Président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé, pour les réformes engagées, sous son impulsion, par le gouvernement, permettant aux femmes de bénéficier d’opportunités croissantes pour leur autonomisation et leur participation au développement national. La porte-parole des groupements bénéficiaires, Mme Sogoyou Bodom a exprimé sa gratitude au gouvernement et son partenaire pour leur soutien. Elle a promis un usage responsable, l’entretien et la gestion des matériels, dans un esprit de solidarité, afin qu’ils profitent, durablement, à toutes les bénéficiaires. ATOP/MEK/DHK/KYA

items.title: Osun election ‘ll expose INEC, security agencies’ 2027 plan — Olawepo-Hashim
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Presidential candidate of the Accord Party, Dr. Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has warned that the forthcoming Osun State governorship election would expose what the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, and security agencies have in store for the 2027 general election, urging President Bola Tinubu to ensure a level playing field in the poll. His warning came as he moved to rally a divided Accord Party in Osun State, accused Governor Ademola Adeleke of betraying the party, rejected calls for political retaliation and urged members and supporters to close ranks, shun anti-party activities and intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the election. Hashim spoke after receiving the report of a seven-member committee of Accord Party stakeholders in Osun State, which consulted widely on recent political developments and briefed him on the state of the party. As he reflected on the committee’s findings, he maintained that despite his grievances against Adeleke, he would not undermine the party’s electoral chances through retaliatory politics. “Osun State election is the major off-season election before 2027. What happens would tell everyone what INEC and Nigeria security forces plan to do in 2027. The world is watching,” Olawepo-Hashim said, while calling on President Tinubu to guarantee a free, fair and credible contest. He insisted that the future of the Accord Party in Osun would be determined by the loyalty and commitment of its members rather than the actions of a few individuals, urging supporters not to lose faith in the party. “Governor Ademola Adeleke has obviously acted as a disloyal Party man, but I will not respond by engaging in anti-party activities in Osun. Two wrongs do not make a right,” Olawepo-Hashim declared. He maintained that his political decisions would continue to be guided by principle, democratic values and his Christian faith rather than bitterness or revenge. “I am a Christian. The Bible teaches that vengeance belongs to the Lord. I have no reason to pursue political revenge,” he added. Olawepo-Hashim, however, hinted that the Adeleke family’s recent political choices may have been shaped by pressures not apparent to the public, saying those realities informed his decision to exercise restraint instead of escalating the political dispute. “The Adeleke family is under pressure that many people do not understand. I understand some of those realities and that is why I have chosen to exercise restraint in my political response. Sometimes politicians take decisions that appear illogical. Supporting President Bola Ahmed Tinubu despite the political pressure the APC has mounted against them is one such example. I am not angry with them; I pity them,” he said. The Accord presidential candidate also reaffirmed his commitment to strengthening the party in Osun and across the country, urging members to deepen grassroots mobilisation as preparations gather pace for the governorship election. “I sincerely appreciate every Accord member, elder and stakeholder in Osun State who has stood firmly with our Party and our Presidential agenda. Your loyalty, sacrifice and courage will never be forgotten or taken for granted,” he said. Olawepo-Hashim assured party faithful that their sacrifices would not be in vain, expressing confidence that the party’s future rested with members who remained committed to its ideals. “The Accord Party belongs to its members. Its future would be determined by the loyalty, commitment and hard work of those who believe in its ideals. I urge every supporter in Osun to remain focused, united and mobilized for victory,” he said. The latest intervention comes amid growing unease within the Accord Party following Governor Adeleke’s repeated endorsement of President Tinubu, a development that has deepened tensions between the governor and supporters of Hashim’s presidential bid ahead of the Osun governorship election. items.title: Osun Election: Ignore threats, vote en masse, Adeleke urges Osun electorate
items.description: By Shina Abubakar OSOGBO — With less than two weeks to the Osun State governorship election, Governor Ademola Adeleke has urged residents not to be intimidated by threats or violence but to come out in large numbers to vote on August 15. Adeleke made the appeal while addressing worshippers during a church service at Winners’ Chapel, Osogbo, on Sunday. In a statement issued by his spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, the governor accused the opposition of being responsible for the violence recorded in the state ahead of the election. According to him, “Because the people have rejected them, because voters have endorsed me, and because defeat stares them in the face, they have resorted to violence. We are not scared. Osun people are not afraid. “On August 15, Osun people will show agents of violence that we are not cowards. Our people’s safety is guaranteed. Come out and vote. Reject those behind violence by voting against them on August 15. “We are not scared of the Osun APC. We have the capacity and the strength, but we care about the safety of our people. My primary goal is the protection and safety of our people. Come out and vote your conscience.” The governor said he was confident of victory, attributing his optimism to what he described as his administration’s achievements in workers’ welfare, healthcare, education, infrastructure, agriculture and other sectors. “Our achievements in workers’ welfare, health, education, infrastructure, agriculture and other sectors speak for us. “I am confident of victory on August 15. We represent the light, and we shall overcome darkness. Osun people must continue to stand up for their democratic rights,” he said. Earlier, the Resident Pastor of Winners’ Chapel, Pastor Adekunle Oluseyi, prayed for the governor, asking God to grant him wisdom and strength in the discharge of his responsibilities. items.title: Yoto/Les festivités de la 11ème édition de la fête ‘’Ahézan’’ lancées à Ahépé
items.description: Tabligbo, 2 août. (ATOP) – Les festivités de la 11 ème édition de la fête identitaire « Ahézan » ont été lancée, le samedi 1 er août à Ahépé, dans la commune Yoto 2 sous le thème « Ahézan : Communion pour l’élévation d’un peuple ». Cette célébration se veut un cadre de retrouvailles, de réflexion et de mobilisation des filles et fils du grand peuple Ahé autour des défis de leur terroir. Il s’agit d’œuvrer pour l’unité, la cohésion sociale et l’engagement collectif pour l’essor du canton. Instituée en 2014, la fête Ahézan est devenue au fil des années le principal rendez-vous culturel des ressortissants du canton d’Ahépé. Au-delà de son caractère festif, elle s’est imposée comme un puissant outil d’intégration local, de valorisation du patrimoine culturel et de réflexion sur les enjeux socio-économiques du milieu. La cheffe canton d’Ahépé lancçant au micho lançant les festivités d’Ahézan édition 2026 Plusieurs activités sont inscrites au programme de cette édition notamment, des messes catholiques, une conférence débat sur le thème « l’élévation d’Ahépé : diagnostic et perspectives », une opération « ville propre », un marathon et une marche populaire. Il y aura aussi des échanges sur la santé par l’alimentation et une retraite aux flambeaux. L’élection de Miss Ahé, des animations populaires, un bal géant ainsi qu’un pique-nique de communion fraternelle destiné à renforcer les liens font également partie du programme. La cérémonie de lancement a été marquée par la présentation du pagne officiel Ahézan 2026 suivie de son acquisition par l’ancêtre Togbui Ahé. Dans un geste hautement symbolique, ce pagne a été nouée à la statue de l’ancêtre Togbui Ahé, traduisant l’attachement du peuple Ahé à son histoire, à ses valeurs culturelles et à son héritage. L’assistance a également suivi une démonstration accompagnée de consignes relatives à la retraite aux flambeaux. En lançant les festivités, la cheffe canton d’Ahépé, Nana Sara Egbewossi Assignon IV a exhorté les populations à participer massivement aux différentes activités inscrites à l’agenda. Elle les a invités à faire de cette édition, un moment de communion, de valorisation de la culture Ahé et de mobilisation pour le développement du canton. Le président du comité d’organisation, Georges Ehli a rappelé que cette fête constitue le socle de la renaissance du peuple Ahé, fruit de la vision et de l’engagement des pionniers qui ont initié cette aventure culturelle. Il a souligné que cette 11 ème édition est bâtie autour de trois piliers stratégiques notamment, la communion culturelle, le développement économique et l’attractivité du territoire, ainsi que l’élévation sociale à travers l’émergence de leaders et le financement de micro-projets visibles. Le maire de la commune Yoto 2, Max Assignon a invité les filles et fils d’Ahépé à demeurer unis, à privilégier la compréhension mutuelle et à consolider la cohésion sociale afin de promouvoir un développement harmonieux inclusif et durable de leur milieu. La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence des autorités administratives, traditionnelles, religieuses, des cadres du canton ainsi que de nombreux filles et fils d’Ahépé venus partager ce moment de retrouvailles et d’espérance. ATOP/SAK/DHK/KYA

items.title: CPPE seeks development finance overhaul to bridge N50trn real sector funding gap
items.description: By Yinka Kolawole The Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise (CPPE) has called for a comprehensive overhaul of Nigeria’s development finance architecture to address an estimated N50 trillion financing gap constraining the country’s productive sectors. In a policy brief issued on Sunday, the Chief Executive Officer of CPPE, Dr. Muda Yusuf, said inadequate access to affordable, long-term finance remains one of the biggest obstacles to growth in manufacturing, agriculture, agribusiness, micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), and export-oriented businesses. According to him, the financing gap reflects deep structural market failures rather than a shortage of liquidity in the financial system. He noted that businesses continue to grapple with high lending rates, short loan tenors and stringent collateral requirements, making it difficult to expand operations, improve productivity and invest in new technologies. Yusuf estimated the real sector financing gap at more than N50 trillion, stressing that agriculture, despite contributing over one-fifth of Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP), has historically attracted less than five per cent of bank credit. He added that manufacturers require affordable, long-term funding for machinery acquisition, factory expansion, technology upgrades, energy infrastructure, automation and export development—investments that cannot be sustainably financed through expensive short-term commercial bank loans. According to him, prevailing monetary conditions, including the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) of 26.5 per cent and the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) of 45 per cent, have further increased borrowing costs, pushing commercial lending rates beyond levels many productive businesses can sustain. While acknowledging the efforts of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to restore monetary policy credibility, stabilise the exchange rate and curb inflation, Yusuf argued that price stability should be complemented by policies that promote investment, job creation and economic growth. “Price stability and development finance should not be treated as mutually exclusive objectives,” he said, adding that transparent and well-targeted development finance interventions can complement monetary policy without fuelling inflation. Yusuf maintained that commercial banks alone cannot finance Nigeria’s industrialisation because they depend largely on short-term deposits. He identified information asymmetry, rigid collateral requirements and government crowding out private-sector borrowers as major constraints to lending. To bridge the financing gap, he called for the recapitalisation of the Bank of Industry and the Bank of Agriculture, expansion of credit guarantee schemes, establishment of longer-tenor refinancing windows, promotion of supply chain financing and cash flow-based lending, strengthening of credit information systems, mobilisation of pension and insurance funds for productive investments, and a reduction in domestic government borrowing. He also stressed the need for stronger governance, transparency and accountability in the implementation of all development finance programmes. items.title: Chelsea sign Argentina’s World Cup star Valentin Barco from Strasbourg
items.description: Valentin Barco became Chelsea’s seventh signing of the transfer window on Sunday after joining from sister club Strasbourg on a seven-year deal. Barco is the second player to join the Blues from the Ligue 1 club this window after Emmanuel Emegha and it is the 13th deal between the two clubs, who share an ownership group, since the start of last season. The 22-year-old was part of the Argentina squad that reached the World Cup final and was involved in an angry exchange with Jude Bellingham for his exuberant celebrations in front of England players during the semi-final. Capable of operating at both left-back and in midfield, Barco had a brief spell in the Premier League previously with Brighton three seasons ago. He moved to Strasbourg initially on loan from the Seagulls in 2024, but signed permanently a year later having helped the club to qualify for the Conference League. Barco’s arrival continues a busy summer in the transfer market for Chelsea as they look to remodel under new boss Xabi Alonso. On Saturday the Blues confirmed the signing of veteran striker Danny Welbeck from Brighton, following the arrivals of Crystal Palace’s Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa. Marco Palestra, Emegha and Geovany Quenda have also been signed. The post Chelsea sign Argentina’s World Cup star Valentin Barco from Strasbourg appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Wuse residents appeal to Wike over prolonged water shortage
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Residents of Wuse District in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) have appealed to the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, to urgently restore public water supply following nearly three weeks of dry taps in Wuse Zones 1, 2, 3 and Wuse II. The residents said the prolonged disruption has subjected households and businesses to severe hardship, forcing many to rely on commercial water vendors at high costs. A resident of Wuse Zone 2, Mrs. Ngozi Okafor, described the situation as unbearable, saying many families now spend a significant portion of their income on buying water. “For almost three weeks now, there has been no water from our taps. Every day we buy water from vendors, and the cost keeps increasing. Water is a basic necessity, and we are appealing to the authorities to restore the supply because we need water urgently,” she said. Another resident, Mr. John Bamgbose of Wuse Zone 6, warned that the prolonged shortage poses serious public health risks. “The situation is becoming a serious health concern. Families are rationing water meant for cooking, bathing and sanitation. We are worried that if nothing is done, people may begin to fall sick. The government should act before diseases break out,” he said. Also speaking, a resident of Wuse II, Mrs. Esther Bassey, urged the FCT Minister, the Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA) and the Federal Capital Development Authority (FCDA) to intervene immediately. “We are appealing to the FCT Minister, the FCTA and the FCDA to come to our rescue. Wuse is one of the major districts in Abuja, and residents should not have to suffer this way. We hope the authorities will listen to our cry and restore water supply without further delay,” she said. The residents called on the relevant authorities to treat the situation as an emergency, stressing that access to clean water is essential for public health, sanitation and residents’ wellbeing. They expressed hope that normal water supply would be restored without further delay to ease the hardship being experienced across the district and prevent possible outbreaks of water-borne diseases. The post Wuse residents appeal to Wike over prolonged water shortage appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kpendjal/football/ Gala communal pour la paix et la cohésion sociale : Les clubs “Kpénadjala” de Mandouri et “Hirondelles” de Kpaporga sacrés vainqueurs
items.description: Mandouri, 2 août (ATOP) – Les clubs “Kpénadjala” du canton de Mandouri (kpendjal1) et “Hirondelles” de Kpaporga du canton de Borgou ont remporté, respectivement les 30 et 31 juillet notamment à Mandouri et Borgou les trophées de la première édition du gala communal, dédié à la promotion de la paix de la cohésion sociale et du vivre ensemble. Ce gala est initié par l’ONG Youth Awake, avec l’appui technique et financier du ministère fédéral des Affaires étrangères de l’Allemagne. Il s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet “de renforcement de l’inclusion et de la résilience des jeunes et des femmes pour lutter contre l’extrémisme violent et le terrorisme, tout en promouvant, l’harmonie sociale et la stabilité (Phase 2). Remise du trophée au capitaine de Kpénadjala Le gala a mobilisé six clubs. Dans Kpendjal 1, la confrontation a opposé, les équipes de “Kpénadjala” de Mandouri, “Chelsea” de Koundjoiré et Tambigou, tandis que dans Kpendjal 2 , la compétition a regroupé “Abeilles rouges” de Bouldjoiré, “Aquatique” de Borgou et “Hirondelles” de Kpaporga. Au terme des matches à élimination directe, Les formations “Kpénadjala” de Mandouri et de Tambigou (Kpendjal 1) et “Aquatique” de Borgou et “Hirondelles” de Kpaporga (Kpendjal 2) ont obtenu leur ticket pour le bouquet final. Les finales disputées en deux mi-temps de trente cinq minutes sur les terrains de Mandouri et Borgou ont été marquées par un rythme soutenu, séduisant qui a enthousiasmé le public sportif. A Mandouri dans Kpendjal 1, Dès le coup d’envoi, la formation de Tambigou communément appelé, “l’autre côté du fleuve kpendjal” a affiché son ambition de remporter le trophée. Il a ouvert le score à la 10 e min de jeu par Abou Allassani suite à un mauvais dégagement de la défense adverse. Une minute plus tard, le club de Kpénadjala réagi et égalise par Yawo. La pause intervient sur le score de 1-1. À la reprise, malgré les occasions de part et d’autre, les attaquants ont manqué de réalisme devant les buts. Score final, un but partout. À l’issue des séances de tirs au but, les joueurs de l’équipe “Kpénadjala” ont été décisifs en marquant 4 tirs contre 2 pour Tambigou . Le capitaine de Hirondelles brandissant le trophée A Borgou dans Kpendjal 2 , la finale s’est achevée sur un score de 0 à 0 malgré des efforts des joueurs observés de part et d’autre. Au terme des séances de tirs au but, l’équipe “Hirondelle” a enregistré 2 tirs contre 1 du côté de “Aquatique”. À la fin du gala, les clubs victorieux “Kpénadjala” de Mandouri et “Hirondelles” de Kpaporga ont reçu de la part des trophées, des ballons et une enveloppe financière. Les autres équipes participantes ont également reçu chacune un ballon ainsi qu’un accompagnement financier. Le Président du Conseil d’administration de Youth Awake, Dambré Sibite a souligné que ce gala constitue un outil puissant de sensibilisation aux valeurs de paix de cohésion sociale et du vivre ensemble. Il a ajouté qu’à travers cette compétition, l’ONG Youth Awake entend faire du sport un levier stratégique pour la consolidation de la paix et le renforcement du tissu social au Togo en général et dans la préfecture de kpendjal en particulier. Le gala a connu la présence des autorités locales et du président du district de football de Kpendjal Issa Yaya. ATOP/BLS/JK/KYA

items.title: Nigeria condoles Algeria over deadly road crash
items.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has expressed condolences to the Government and people of Algeria following a road accident in Boumerdès Province that claimed 27 lives and left more than 40 others injured. In a statement issued on Sunday, the Spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kimiebi Imomotimi Ebienfa, said Nigeria was deeply saddened by the bus crash, which occurred near El Karma while the vehicle was travelling from Sétif to Algiers on Friday, July 31, 2026. The Federal Government also acknowledged the declaration of three days of national mourning by Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune in honour of the victims. Nigeria said it stands in solidarity with Algeria during the period of mourning and shares the country’s grief over the loss of lives. The government extended its condolences to the families of the victims and prayed for the peaceful repose of those who died in the crash. It also wished the injured a speedy recovery and expressed confidence in the resilience of the Algerian people as they recover from the tragedy. items.title: Labour Party to opposition groups: Join us, we’re the real coalition
items.description: …Says nationwide NLC, TUC structures give it edge By John Alechenu ABUJA — The Labour Party (LP) has urged opposition groups and political movements to shelve plans for new alliances and instead align with its platform ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party said it already possesses the strongest nationwide structure capable of unseating the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). This was contained in a statement issued on Sunday in Abuja by the party’s National Publicity Secretary, Ken Asogwa. According to the LP, while it supports broad-based collaboration among opposition forces, creating new political platforms or fragmented alliances would only weaken the opposition. Asogwa said the Labour Party already represents the most viable platform for a united opposition. “While the Labour Party appreciates the need for broad-based collaboration among opposition forces to democratically unseat the ruling All Progressives Congress, the party maintains that its platform already represents the strongest and most organically structured coalition capable of winning a presidential election in Nigeria. “The Labour Party is unique among all political parties because the Nigeria Labour Congress and the Trade Union Congress are its institutional members. By implication, every serving and retired civil servant across the country is naturally connected to the Labour Party family through these labour institutions. “That gives the Labour Party an unrivalled grassroots presence. There is hardly any polling unit, ward, local government or community in Nigeria that does not have a serving or retired civil servant. No other political party, including the APC, can genuinely boast of such an extensive nationwide structure.” The party called on individuals and groups advocating a grand opposition coalition to strengthen the Labour Party instead of establishing new platforms. According to the statement, “Rather than creating new platforms or fragmented alliances, the national interest would be better served by strengthening the one opposition party that already possesses a tested nationwide network and institutional foundation.” The LP also said it has a formidable organisational structure, an energised membership base and “a credible presidential candidate who is young, well-educated and possesses the capacity to provide the visionary leadership Nigerians seek.” “It would therefore be politically unwise to sacrifice such enormous institutional advantages on the altar of an unnecessary coalition arrangement,” the party added. Asogwa maintained that the opposition’s task ahead of the 2027 elections is not to create another platform but to unite behind what he described as the most viable existing platform. “The task before the opposition is not to reinvent the wheel but to unite behind the most viable platform. That platform is the Labour Party,” he said. The post Labour Party to opposition groups: Join us, we’re the real coalition appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Second phase of AJK polls concludes amid renewed rigging allegations by PPP
items.description: The second phase of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections took place on Sunday, with polling held in eight out of the nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division and all 12 refugee constituencies. Polling began at 8am and continued till 5pm for the refugee seats, while the process concluded at 6pm in Muzaffarabad after an hour-long extension. The electoral process in LA-27 (Muzaffarabad-I) was postponed due to heavy rain, AJK Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal said, DawnNewsTV reported . Polling in LA-27, commonly known as Kutla, was deferred until August 4 after polling material could not be dispatched due to a landslide. Similarly, polling in 52 of the 147 polling stations of LA-28 (Muzaffarabad-II) was also postponed until August 4 for the same reason. Over 300 candidates were in the fray for the Muzaffarabad seats and the 12 seats for refugees settled in different regions. Continuing his rigging allegations, PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Sunday accused the PML-N of “robbing” votes in the second phase of the AJK elections as well. In a post on X later in the day, he condemned an “attack” on the party’s regional president, Chaudhry Latif Akbar — also the candidate for LA-31 (Muzaffarabad-V). Accusing “miscreant elements of the PML-N” of being behind the incident, Bilawal said PPP worker Mushtaq Shah was killed in the same constituency. “The PML-N is robbing the votes of the people of Azad Kashmir through bullets, batons and coercion,” he alleged. The PPP chairman demanded that those responsible for the attack on Akbar and the “murderers” of the party worker be arrested immediately. In a separate statement , Bilawal said, “The PML-N has crossed all limits. Attacks are taking place on our voters and the president of the state (AJK).” He remarked that in Muzaffarabad, the PPP’s “politics of dignity and principles was in contest with the PML-N’s threat, rigging and coercion”. The PPP shared a complaint written to the Election Commission regarding a “physical assault” on Akbar. The party said the LA-31 candidate was “engaged in the electoral process on polling day” when the alleged incident took place, accusing three individuals. It said a first information report (FIR) was being registered and urged the Election Commission to order an inquiry into the “security lapse” that resulted in the incident. AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, who belongs to the PPP, took notice of the incident and ordered the chief secretary and the police chief to take those responsible to justice. The AJK PM termed the attack “a slap on the politics of dignity and principle in Kashmir”. Akbar also wrote two letters to the Election Commission. In one, he alleged that an attempt on his life was made at Polling Station 177 “by PML-N workers” and wrote of the PPP worker’s death. He further claimed that his polling agents were not allowed to “sit in the polling area” at 14 polling stations. In the second letter, Akbar said PPP leader Syed Mumtaz Hussain Naqvi sustained bullet wounds in a “[murderous] attack” at a polling station in a building. Addressing a press conference, PPP leader Nayyar Hussain Bokhari claimed that eight party workers had been injured in the ongoing elections so far. Bokhari contended there was a “state of lawlessness” in AJK. Polls in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with the first set of polls held in Mirpur division on July 27, the second held today, and the third phase set for August 10 across Poonch division. Ahead of today’s elections, internet services were restored in parts of Muzaffarabad division after remaining suspended for 54 days on July 29. At the time, it was not clear whether the restoration covered the entire division or was limited to the state capital. Addressing the media on Sunday, the AJK CEC said that a letter had been written yesterday to request the restoration of internet services. He added that the outcome would be known today, without providing further details. “We will work according to the law; we will not come under pressure from anyone,” CEC Mughal said to a question. Preliminary, unofficial results According to preliminary and unofficial results, the PML-N was leading in LA-25 by 1,364 votes, while the PPP was ahead in LA-26 and LA-28 by 1,745 and 1,782 votes, respectively. In LA-29, the PML-N was leading by 379 votes, with the PPP in second place. Similarly, the PML-N was ahead in LA-30 by 247 votes, while the PPP was trailing in second position. In LA-31, the PML-N was leading with 2,934 votes, while the PPP was in second place. In LA-32, the PML-N was ahead by 892 votes, according to the unofficial results. In LA-33, the PPP was leading by 1,349 votes, while the PML-N was ahead in LA-34 with a lead of 2,503 votes. Refugee seats CEC Mughal held a press conference along with senior Election Commission members Khawaja Muhammad Ahsan and Syed Nazirul Hassan Gilani. “The second phase of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly elections is being completed today,” the CEC said. He said the results from the five refugee seats had been received, with PML-N candidates winning four of the five seats, while the PPP secured one seat. PML-N’s Muhammad Amir Shah won LA-41 (Kashmir Valley-II) with 1,804 votes, defeating independent candidate Saba Diwan, who secured 1,523 votes. In LA-42 (Kashmir Valley-III), PML-N candidate Syed Shaukat Ali Shah emerged victorious with 1,524 votes, while PPP’s Muhammad Asim Sharif received 466 votes. PML-N’s Muhammad Yasin Loon won LA-43 (Kashmir Valley-IV) with 1,276 votes, defeating PPP candidate Javed Butt, who secured 563 votes. In LA-44 (Kashmir Valley-V), PML-N candidate Muhammad Ahmad Raza Qadri won with 2,308 votes, while All Jammu and Kashmir Muslim Conference candidate Mehrun Nisa received 740 votes. The PPP secured LA-45 (Kashmir Valley-VI), where Abdul Majid Khan won with 3,448 votes, defeating Muslim Conference candidate Khawaja Muhammad Dilawar, who obtained 823 votes. Info ministry criticises foreign media coverage The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting criticised Al Jazeera’s coverage of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections, accusing the channel of “selective reporting” from “handpicked polling stations” in Muzaffarabad. In a post on X, the ministry alleged that the channel had sought to “misrepresent” the elections and voting process through “carefully chosen timings and scripted statements from selected individuals”. It alleged that it was aimed at “delegitimising” the electoral exercise and undermining the will of the people of Muzaffarabad and AJK. PML-N says man did not die from bullet, had heart failure On its part, the PML-N disputed the PPP’s stance on a man’s death in Muzaffarabad, saying that he died due to heart failure and did not suffer any bullet injury. Responding to the PPP’s stream of allegations in a media talk in Rawalpindi, PML-N Punjab Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb said a man aged between 68 and 70 years was trying to resolve a “scuffle” when he suffered heart failure. She noted that there was a physical altercation between groups of the PML-N and the PPP, describing the incident as “unfortunate”. She further said that Shah’s family has refused to have a post-mortem examination conducted. “Will you do politics on bullets? Will you sabotage a democratic process by spreading such fake claims?” Aurangzeb said. She further said, “My brothers, this politics of bullet, this politics of robbing votes, this does not suit parties like us.” The PML-N leader went on to emphasise that the PPP leadership had given sacrifices and spent their “entire lives” in making efforts to strengthen democracy. She remarked that ex-prime minister Benazir Bhutto “did not give sacrifice to see this day”. “You should remember that you are Zulfikar Ali Bhutto’s grandson. We will keep reminding you because we will not let their sacrifices go to waste.” She further said that the PPP was aware that the public did not vote for it. “Are elections won by crying, grabbing collars, issuing threats or making accusations? Elections are won with courage.” The PML-N leader also took exception to Bilawal’s remarks of “snatching away seats” and “taking out seats”, saying: “Bilawal, you say good things. What kind of statements are you making now?” Aurangzeb compared the PPP’s attitude to that of the PTI, saying the former’s “narrative” should not be the same. “Find out so that you may not have to cry in Sindh,” the PML-N leader cautioned the PPP, noting people in Sindh were seeking performance similar to that of the Punjab government. Aurangzeb recalled the Charter of Democracy signed between the PPP and the PML-N in 2007, stressing that its purpose was not to let democratic processes be sabotaged. Noting that the PPP was in power in AJK and had its administrative machinery in the region, the PML-N leader questioned if Bilawal’s “own government is carrying out rigging against you”. She remarked that if one considered the PPP’s allegations to be true, the party would have to “accept” that its own government “carried out rigging against Bilawal”. Aurangzeb said the PPP-led administration was preventing the transportation of the required electoral equipment. She also commented on Bokhari showing ballot papers stamped with votes for PML-N, saying, “This is an election of thousands of votes. He was showing two stamps on two ballot papers.” The Punjab minister took aim at the PPP’s governance, saying that it had nothing to show for its performance. She quipped that voters were yet to head to polling stations early in the morning while the PPP had already started holding media talks on rigging. Aurangzeb said that if the PPP still had reservations, there were relevant platforms such as the Election Commission and tribunals to approach, rather than hold press conferences. “Contest the elections. Do not cry out loud,” she said. In a similar tone, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah also regretted the rigging allegations levelled by the PPP. “Unfortunately, a democratic party, which is also a signatory to the Charter of Democracy, has been alleging rigging since 10:30 in the morning,” he said while addressing the media in Islamabad. Flanked by Kashmir Affairs Minister Amir Muqam, Sanaullah claimed that the second phase of polls in AJK was conducted in a “peaceful manner”. The inter-provincial coordination minister said the electoral process was completed at 96 per cent of polling stations, adding that vote counting was underway. Sanaullah maintained that it was the “most transparent and non-violent electoral process”, adding that a few incidents had occurred during the day. Referring to the alleged attack on PPP leader Akbar, Sanaullah said it was a dispute involving another family in the area and that there had been “no physical confrontation”, only a verbal argument. Contesting the PPP’s claim about the second reported incident involving a party worker, the PML-N leader said a citizen named Mushtaq was involved in a scuffle with his family members, one of whom pushed him. “He reportedly went home afterwards and then suffered a heart attack as he was a cardiac patient. They [PPP] claimed that shots were fired, but not a single bullet was fired,” the premier’s adviser asserted. Sanaullah added that the PML-N condoled his death, but that the “deceased individual was not a PPP worker”. PPP alleges electoral malpractices On Sunday, the PPP alleged electoral malpractices shortly after polling commenced, with several of the complaints claiming its polling agents at some stations were not allowed to observe the voting process. At 2pm, the party also wrote a separate letter to the Election Commission requesting follow-up on 25 complaints filed by it regarding 11 constituencies. The PPP said it had not received any formal written response or acknowledgement from the electoral watchdog on the status of any of the 25 complaints. “Given the gravity, number and geographical spread of the violations documented, the Party respectfully submits that a formal response from the Commission is now overdue and urgently required.” On the other hand, the PML-N’s social media posts revolved around voters across Muzaffarabad and Punjab showing up to cast ballots with “ enthusiasm ”. Several posts highlighted that a large number of voters were flocking to the PML-N’s election camps, rather than those of rival parties. The PML-N also wrote to the Election Commission in response to a PPP complaint about LA-40 (Valley-I), terming the latter’s allegations against its candidate Muhammad Naeem Khan as “baseless”. In the letter, seen by Dawn , the PML-N asserted that the allegations “regarding administrative failures are unsubstantiated and appear to be an attempt to create unnecessary controversy around the polling process”. The PML-N urged the electoral watchdog to ensure that “no misleading or politically motivated complaint is allowed to undermine public confidence in the integrity of the polling”. ‘Ballot stuffing’ At a polling station in LA-32 (Muzaffarabad-VI), the PPP accused PML-N supporters of “ballot stuffing”. It further said that a government employee had been deployed as a polling agent for the PML-N at a separate polling station. In LA-30 (Muzaffarabad-IV), the PPP claimed PML-N workers removed a ballot box at the Banaw Langah polling station and placed it outside, where they were allegedly “stamping ballot papers”. In Charakhpora Union Council of LA-31 (Muzaffarabad-V), the PPP said “bogus voting” was taking place at the Sharik Kamal Bandi-Khalsa polling station. The party said the alleged act “directly subverts the integrity of the poll”, adding that the polling station also did not have adequate security despite being declared “sensitive”. The PPP also alleged a PML-N MPA at a polling station in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Abbottabad of obstructing the voting process for the refugee seat of LA-45 (Kashmir-VI). In LA-25 (Neelum-I), the PPP said the voting process at a polling station had been halted after reports emerged of PML-N supporters tearing up ballot papers. The PPP also said its polling agents at a polling station in LA-25’s Khawaja Sari reported that “fraudulent votes are being cast” there. It urged the Election Commission to dispatch officials and law enforcement to halt the alleged action. ‘Polling agents excluded’ The party alleged that its polling agents were not allowed to sit at polling stations for refugee seat LA-34 (Jammu-I) in Cantonment and Lahore’s Sheranwala Gate, calling on the Election Commission to intervene. The PPP wrote to the electoral watchdog about a similar complaint emerging from a polling station in Janabad, Sargodha, for LA-34. Sharing another letter addressed to the Election Commission about LA-34, the PPP said “elected members” of the PML-N were present inside a Pakpattan polling station and “stamping ballot papers”. It further claimed that its polling agent was “barred from entering the same polling station”. “The deliberate exclusion of the PPP’s oversight representative while PML-N’s own elected officials conduct fraud inside the station is not a coincidence — it is a coordinated strategy to commit electoral fraud without any independent witness,” it alleged. The party urged the electoral watchdog to dispatch law enforcement to the polling station and remove the PML-N supporters allegedly involved in “ballot stuffing”. Regarding LA-42 (Valley-III), the PPP filed a complaint over party candidate Asim Sharif Butt’s polling agent being “physically prevented” from entering a polling station in Muzaffargarh’s Alipur Tehsil. The PPP also claimed its polling agents at three polling stations in LA-30 (Muzaffarabad-IV) were denied from observing the electoral process. Similarly, the party said polling agents of candidate Ishfaq Zaffar were not permitted to take their seats at three polling stations in LA-32 (Muzaffarabad-VI). Terming it a “serious violation” of the electoral code of conduct, the PPP sought disciplinary action against the presiding officers who allegedly refused the agents from discharging their duties. At one of those polling stations, the PPP claimed a “violent confrontation” was underway between supporters of PML-N candidate Raja Farooq Haider and PPP supporters. Other issues In a separate statement in the morning, the party claimed that no polling staff was present at any of the 196 polling stations in LA-27, adding that this raised the concern that there was a “deliberate” attempt to delay the polling. Similarly, the party alleged that polling staff had reached late at 71 polling stations of LA-28, due to which the voting process was facing delays. The PPP claimed that a similar situation was being witnessed at several polling stations of LA-30, where polling staff had not arrived on time. Regarding LA-31, the PPP said it had written to the Election Commission on behalf of its candidate Akbar, urging it to take action over difficulties faced by voters due to the closure of the Rangla-Katkair Road in Muzaffarabad. The party said over 50 vehicles carrying voters were stuck due to the road’s closure. PML-N slams ‘blame game’ Earlier in the day, PML-N’s Muqam called on political parties not to indulge in a “blame game”. “Nothing is to be gained from a blame game,” he said during a press conference in Islamabad, adding that law enforcement personnel were also deployed to ensure security. “They should not act in a manner that ‘why was I not given seats’,” Muqam said, stressing that it was the public whose votes allocate seats. The minister urged all political parties to let the electoral process take place in a peaceful manner, stressing that making allegations without evidence cannot change the results. At the same time, Muqam also highlighted “arbitrary transfers and administrative decisions” in AJK, where the PPP is in power. He said the moves “seemed discriminatory”. He recalled that the PML-N had accepted the results of elections in Gilgit-Baltistan held in June, where the PPP emerged the winner and formed the government. Defending the results from Mirpur, Muqam asserted that the people voted for PML-N due to its performance. On the other hand, PPP leader Nadeem Afzal Chan also held a press conference where he called on the Election Commission to play its role in “proving” the election process in AJK to be free and fair. “Azad Kashmir is an international issue … people’s eyes are on it,” the former MNA said, adding that if the commission did not recognise the public and assure a free election, “tomorrow we will not be able to ratify this election under any circumstance”. He recalled that after the Mirpur polls, there was a detailed discussion within the party about boycotting the second and third phases. However, the party leadership refused the idea of a boycott. Chan cautioned that if the PPP was “compelled” to move towards such steps for the third phase, it would benefit those who wanted to prove the election “dirty”. “I see this becoming an ultra Form-47 election,” he said. He said that in negotiations in Muzaffarabad, the PPP had provided proof of rigging in four constituencies, as well as agreeing to hold re-polling in any other constituencies in which there were objections. He also called for a benchmark for voting, saying, “General polling was less than 30 per cent. But wherever you won, it was 80pc, 90pc, 75pc … this doesn’t even happen in urban cities like Islamabad and Lahore.” ‘Admission of rigging’ The PPP and the PML-N — coalition partners in the Centre — have been engaged in a war of words since the PML-N emerged in the lead during the first phase of polls. The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging in Mirpur and demanded re-polling. Scuffles, violence and allegations of rigging had marred the polls in Mirpur, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice. To defuse the tensions, senior leaders of both parties met multiple times in Azad Kashmir over the weekend to “explore a legal resolution” to the dispute. The latest round of talks followed two earlier meetings on Thursday and Friday. A PML-N source told Dawn that discussions focused on the PPP’s allegations and its demand for re-polling in certain constituencies. “It was not planned or pre-planned rigging but isolated acts at places where supporters of one candidate enjoyed numerical dominance over their opponents. Such incidents have unfortunately been part of the territory’s polling atmosphere and have also been witnessed in previous elections,” the source quoted the PML-N leaders as telling their counterparts. Referring to this statement in a X post on Sunday, Bilawal said: “Despite this admission from the rigging party, the [EC] has still failed to take action on our complaints from phase 1. Had they done so, the credibility of today’s phase 2 election would have been restored. “The PPP reserves the right to protest and demand re-election in phases where rigging took place, and the election commission failed to act. We have already sent multiple written complaints about ballot stuffing and illegal removal of our polling agents in today’s election. It is hoped the election commission acts swiftly and at least maintains fairness in round 2.” According to the sources, during meetings with the PML-N, PPP initially raised objections to the results in four constituencies — Charhoi, Sehnsa and Nakyal in Kotli district, and Barnala in Bhimber district during phase-I of the election. However, it later withdrew its allegations regarding Sehnsa and Barnala. Saturday’s discussions centred on Charhoi, where PPP AJK President Chaudhry Yasin lost to PML-N’s Raja Riasat, and Nakyal, where PPP candidate Javed Iqbal Budhanvi was defeated by PML-N’s Raja Ayaz Ahmed. Meanwhile, the Sharif family also held discussions at Jati Umra. According to a statement issued by the PM’s Office, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif held consultations with his elder brother and PML-N chief Nawaz Sharif at Jati Umra to take stock of mounting political challenges, including the rift with the PPP over the AJK elections. A senior PML-N leader told Dawn that the party leadership had taken serious note of the PPP chairman’s increasingly combative rhetoric against the Sharif family over the AJK polls and his warning that the PPP could reconsider its support for the federal government if the remaining phases of the elections were manipulated in favour of the PML-N. Election numbers According to the AJK Election Commission, 207 candidates are in the fray for the nine constituencies in Muzaffarabad division, comprising five seats in Muzaffarabad district and two each in Neelum and Jhelum Valley districts. Another 137 candidates are contesting the 12 refugee constituencies, including six seats representing refugees from the Kashmir Valley and six from Jammu. A total of 809,621 voters are registered in Muzaffarabad division, while the 12 refugee constituencies have a combined electorate of 438,834. According to the commission, 1,483 polling stations have been established across Muzaffarabad division, of which 533 have been declared highly sensitive, 741 sensitive and 209 normal. Another 1,057 polling stations have been set up for the 12 refugee constituencies. Out of 12 refugee seats, seven seats are in Punjab, one seat is in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, one seat (Jammu-VI) is divided between Pun­jab, Islamabad and KP, one seat is divided between Sindh and Balo­chistan (Valley-I), and one seat (Jammu-I) is shared among refugees living in Balochistan, Punjab and Sindh. Valley-V seat is divided between Punjab and Islamabad. In Rawalpindi and Islamabad, about 27,000 registered male and female voters will elect lawmakers for LA-43 (Valley-IV), LA-44 (Valley-V), and LA-39 (Jammu-VI) seats. A total of 175 polling stations have been established, out of which 18 polling stations in Rawalpindi have been declared sensitive. A total of 34 candidates are in the fray. In Gujrat, almost 2,000 policemen will perform security duties at scores of polling stations for the LA-38 elections . The total number of polling stations in these districts is 115, with 75 in Gujrat, 24 in Wazirabad and 16 in Mandi Bahauddin. The total number of voters is 50,225 in the entire constituency. As many as 11 candidates are contesting this seat. In Sindh, officials said the elections will be conducted on LA-34 (Jammu-I) and LA-40 (Kashmir Valley-I) with polling stations established across Karachi and other districts of Sindh. In LA-34 (Jammu-I), a total of 17 candidates are contesting the election, which has 698 registered voters in Karachi’s seven districts and 477 voters in 13 other districts of Sindh. For LA-40 Kashmir (Valley-I), 11 candidates are in the race. The constituency has 4,200 registered voters in Karachi and 403 voters in 17 other districts of Sindh. In Balochistan, seven polling booths have been established across the province for the Kashmir Valley-I constituency, where 1,174 registered voters are expected to cast their ballots. Balochistan shares this seat with Sindh. For the Jammu-I constituency, six polling booths have been set up, with a total of 182 registered voters, including 85 men and 97 women, eligible to vote. Polling stations have been established for AJK refugee voters residing in Balochistan at various locations, including Quetta, Pishin, Qila Saifullah, Hub, Loralai, Sibi, Mastung, Zhob and Barkhan. In KP, 41 polling stations, mostly in Swat and Mansehra, have been set up for the LA-45 (Kashmir VI) seat. Additional input by Ameer Hamza and Tariq Naqash

items.title: Tchaoudjo/inclusion socio-sportive des personnes handicapées : L’association JEC forme des acteurs clés à Lama-Téssi
items.description: Sokodé, 2 août (ATOP) – Un atelier de formation des acteurs clés sur l’importance de l’implication et de la participation des personnes handicapées aux activités sportives et les techniques d’organisation inclusive d’activités sportives adaptées s’est tenu, le samedi 1ᵉʳ août à Lama-Tessi, dans la commune Tchaoudjo 2. Cette formation a été initiée par l’association Jeunesse et engagement citoyen Togo (JEC-Togo). Elle s’inscrit dans le cadre de son projet « Inclusion socio-sportive des personnes handicapées de la commune Tchaoudjo 2 ». Ce projet est mis en œuvre, en synergie, avec l’association Monde Radieux et ladite commune. Il bénéficie de l’appui financier et technique de la Conférence des ministres de la jeunesse et des sports de la francophonie (CONFEJES). Cet atelier a permis de renforcer les capacités de 30 acteurs sportifs du public et du privé et des leaders communautaires sur la pratique du sport adapté en vue de promouvoir la participation et l’inclusion des personnes handicapées dans les activités sportives. Le projet a été présenté aux autorités communales, aux leaders traditionnels et religieux ainsi qu’aux représentants des bénéficiaires finaux. La rencontre a servi de cadre pour faire connaître l’importance de l’inclusion des personnes handicapées dans la pratique du sport aux participants. Elle a donné lieu à des réflexions sur les mesures à prendre pour favoriser la participation effective des personnes handicapées à la pratique du sport. Cette assise a édifié chacun sur son rôle dans la promotion du sport adapté aux personnes en situation de handicap. La coordinatrice de JEC-Togo, Mme Kataba Ali Nwa Leya, a souligné qu’en dépit de ses avantages innombrables, le sport demeure une discipline non accessible à tout le monde, surtout aux personnes handicapées qui sont généralement laissées pour compte. Elle a affirmé que cette situation a des répercussions négatives sur le bien-être intégral de ces personnes marginalisées. Selon elle, la promotion de la pratique inclusive du sport (sport adapté) serait la solution idoine pour favoriser l’implication, la participation des personnes handicapées à la pratique du sport, d’où cette formation à leur endroit. L’adjoint au maire de la commune Tchaoudjo 2, Batayam Agbeton, a relevé l’intérêt du projet qui contribuera à promouvoir d’ici à octobre 2026 l’inclusion sportive et sociale des personnes handicapées dans la commune. Il a réitéré la disponibilité de la mairie à jouer sa partition pour le succès du projet. Les participants ont salué cette initiative et promis de relayer les informations reçues une fois retournés dans leurs communautés. Le projet prévoit, entre autres, des activités impliquant les personnes handicapées, notamment un éco-jogging, des Olympiades et un match de football suivi d’une sensibilisation. Il intègre des émissions radiophoniques et un plaidoyer au niveau de la commune pour dégager une ligne budgétaire en vue de promouvoir les activités sportives des personnes handicapées. ATOP/MEK/MD/KYA

items.title: ₦365m up for grabs as FG rolls out biggest student research prize
items.description: …Directs universities, polytechnics to set up selection panels By John Alechenu ABUJA — The Federal Government has launched the 2026 edition of the Tertiary Institutions National Laureate Programme, with a total prize pool of ₦365 million to reward outstanding student research across tertiary institutions. The Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, is backing the initiative, which will recognise outstanding undergraduate projects, master’s theses and doctoral research from universities, polytechnics, colleges of education, monotechnics and military institutions. The Chairman of the National Laureate Committee, Emeritus Prof. Abubakar Sambo, announced the commencement of this year’s programme in a letter dated July 31, 2026, addressed to vice-chancellors, rectors, provosts and commandants. The announcement was contained in a statement issued on Sunday in Abuja by the committee’s spokesperson, Ita Ekpeyong. As part of the exercise, all participating institutions have been directed to establish Institutional Laureate Selection Committees comprising senior academics. The names of the chairman, secretary and members of each committee are to be submitted to the National Laureate Committee. Professional bodies have also been requested to nominate experts to serve on Regional Laureate Committees that will vet entries. Each institution may nominate a maximum of 18 entries, comprising six undergraduate dissertations, six master’s theses and six doctoral theses. Equivalent categories will apply to polytechnics and colleges of education. Eligible entries must fall within six thematic areas: Agriculture; Teaching Innovation; Medicine and Health; Engineering; Science and Technology; and Law, Arts and Social Sciences. The programme offers prizes of ₦35 million for the best undergraduate research, ₦50 million for the best master’s thesis and ₦100 million for the best doctoral research. In addition, 15 Thematic Awards of ₦12 million each will be presented. To ensure transparency and maintain research standards, all nominated works must first be uploaded to the Nigeria Education Repository and Databank (NERD) and assigned a National Document Number (NDN). Prof. Sambo said the requirement is intended to protect the integrity of academic research and preserve a comprehensive record of Nigerian scholarship. According to him, the selection process will be conducted in three stages—at the institutional, regional and national levels. He urged institutions to ensure transparency in their internal screening processes, adding that each institution’s NERD Focal Officer would activate its panel on the Laureate portal to manage submissions. The deadline for submitting the names of committee members is August 15, 2026, while entries must be submitted on or before August 31, 2026. Describing the initiative as “a landmark investment in intellectual capital,” Prof. Sambo said the programme was designed to promote research excellence, encourage innovation and reward scholars whose work has the potential to transform industries. He urged vice-chancellors and heads of tertiary institutions to provide the leadership needed to ensure the success of the programme’s maiden edition. The post ₦365m up for grabs as FG rolls out biggest student research prize appeared first on Vanguard News .
